office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering the tax structure, water and agriculture policy, K-12 policy and funding, and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: An open seat, vacated by Rep. Alex Ybarra's Senate run, between two Republicans: former Moses Lake council member and nurse Deanna Martinez and Ellensburg council member Joshua Thompson. Both oppose the 2026 income tax; Martinez leads on repealing it and the Climate Commitment Act and on local control, while Thompson runs as a constitutional conservative with platform planks on parents' rights and girls' sports.

candidates.summary: Registered nurse of 30-plus years and former Moses Lake City Council member, raised in Warden, endorsed by several sitting Republican legislators.
highlights: Top priority is abolishing the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, which she calls unconstitutional [S1]
Pledges to work to repeal the Climate Commitment Act [S1]
Puts returning local control first among her priorities and opposes the new sheriff-oversight board [S7][S10]
Would restore state Medicaid funding by redirecting budget dollars, without new taxes [S6]

taxes.basis: Statement and questionnaire both make abolishing the income tax and cutting taxes her top priorities.

spending.basis: Wants to identify waste and get spending under control before any tax increase and to reallocate existing spending; also proposes restoring Medicaid funding.

housing.basis: Would repeal regulations that add to building costs, naming shrub-steppe and urban growth area restrictions; describes 'state goals with local flexibility.'

safety.basis: Lists public safety and law enforcement as priorities; no specific enforcement or prevention proposals.

climate.basis: Pledges to work to repeal the Climate Commitment Act, citing gas prices and rural costs; one explicit statement.

experience.basis: No legislative service; former city council member and former campaign assistant to the seat's incumbent, endorsed by sitting legislators and stressing work with the majority.

local-control.basis: Repeatedly names returning control to local governments as her first priority and opposes the state sheriff-oversight board as a local decision.

healthcare.basis: Would restore state Medicaid funding and expand the nursing workforce through the RN compact, within the existing system.

social.basis: Her priorities page says she will 'protect girls' sports'; a one-line plank.

candidates.summary: Ellensburg City Council member, technology and marketing consultant and Kittitas County Republican precinct officer, endorsed by the Grant, Kittitas and Douglas County Republican parties.
highlights: Calls for cutting taxes "dramatically" and opposes new income taxes [S2][S3]
Says parents' rights "are being dissolved" and objects to boys competing in girls' sports [S2]
Blames regulation and "green mandates" for housing costs; backs duplexes, fourplexes and cottage housing [S2][S4]
Sees technology and AI industries as the district's biggest growth opportunity [S4]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet, website and questionnaire all call for reducing taxes and opposing an income tax; website says to cut taxes dramatically.

spending.basis: Says Washington has a spending problem and calls himself a fiscal hawk; no specific audit or cut proposals.

housing.basis: Attributes the housing shortage to regulation and green mandates, pledges to lower building costs, and backs more missing-middle housing types.

safety.basis: Repeatedly backs law enforcement and more officers per capita, while also naming the fentanyl and mental-health crises.

climate.basis: Criticizes 'absurd green mandates' and calls for protecting dams and new energy policies; no specific climate-law pledge.

experience.basis: No legislative service; a sitting city council member running to 'challenge and change the status quo' and 'not represent the system.'

local-control.basis: Says decisions should stay closer to local communities and pledges to protect local control; secondary in his platform.

social.basis: Platform objects to boys competing in girls' sports and locker rooms.

parental-rights.basis: Platform says parents' rights are being dissolved and limited in public schools and lists parents' rights as a family priority.

tech.basis: Calls technology and AI industries the district's biggest economic opportunity, balanced with natural-resource protection.
